title: Computational Innovation for Genome Editing in Discovery and Therapy
text:
CRISPR genome editing enables precise changes to DNA, helping us understand how genes influence health
and disease, and opening the door to personalized, permanent treatments for disease. My research develops
computational tools that use cutting-edge technologies to measure and interpret these DNA changes accurately.
By making genome editing experiments easier to understand and more reliable, this work will broaden CRISPR’s
impact in both research and clinical care.

title: Cancer Patient on a Chip
text:
Metastatic cancer disease, the leading cause of death in patients with solid tumors, is difficult to study, both in
experimental models and in patients. We propose to establish, utilize and make available a patient-specific model
of breast cancer metastasis. In the renewal phase, our focus will be on cancer-immune interactions during
metastatic progression that can lead to novel strategies for inhibiting metastasis.

title: Sequence resolution of complex human genome structural variation
text:
This proposal focuses on the discovery, sequencing, and characterization of more complex structural variation
that has been difficult to assemble as part of long-read sequencing efforts. The work will help complete our
understanding of the full spectrum of human genetic variation and develop methods to better define complex
patterns of normal variation and their relationship to rearrangements associated with rare pediatric disease.

title: Defining Microbial and Host Pathways Driving Asymptomatic C. difficile Colonization Associated with Aging and High-Sugar Diets
text:
Clostridioides difficile can asymptomatically colonize individuals, particularly those consuming high-sugar
diets or of advanced age, creating a hidden reservoir for transmission and disease. This research will
identify the microbial and host mechanisms that enable asymptomatic carriage and inform new strategies to
prevent CDI through dietary, microbial, or immunological interventions. The findings will support the
development of new strategies to prevent infection and reduce disease transmission, aligning with NIH’s
mission to improve public health.

title: Regulation of epigenome stability by SIRT6 during Aging
text:
Genome architecture deteriorates during aging contributing to age-related pathologies. In this proposal we
outline research related to one gene, SIRT6, which has been implicated as a regulator of mammalian life and
health-spans; here we will investigate the molecular mechanisms by which SIRT6 maintains genome
architecture. We are optimistic that our research will generate novel insights into the aging process and lead to
therapeutic strategies designed to attenuate age-related diseases.

title: Focused Ultrasound and CAR T Cells for Pediatric Brain Malignancies
text:
Medulloblastoma (MB) is the most common pediatric brain tumor and treatment of patients with high-risk
subtypes remains notoriously difficult due to disease complexity, its challenging niche within the immunologically-
and pharmacologically-privileged central nervous system, and the significant risk of long-term developmental
deficits due to treatment toxicities. To this end, promising novel treatment options such as cellular
immunotherapy have not yet found broad success in this disease setting. Our proposal leverages image-guided
focused ultrasound intervention as a novel non-invasive, non-ionizing strategy for augmenting targeted cellular
delivery and persistence in high-risk MB.

title: Accurate High-Resolution Tissue Characterization for Breast Cancer Screening Using Transmission and Reflection Ultrasound Tomography
text:
The proposed research aims to expand the capability and performance of ultrasound tomography as an
imaging modality that enables greater sensitivity and specificity for breast cancer screening without using
compression or ionizing radiation. To achieve this goal, we plan to improve the modeling and inversion
techniques currently used in ultrasound tomography to better accommodate high-frequency signals, thereby
increasing the achievable imaging resolution and accuracy of ultrasound tomography. Successful completion of
this project will improve fundamental understandings of acoustic models and inversion techniques for reflection
and transmission ultrasound and enable the quantitative imaging of tissue properties at higher spatial resolution
for the early detection and diagnosis of cancer.

title: Next Generation IgH-reprogramming for in vivo delivery
text: Genome-modified B cells are promising as functional cure for HIV since they can be used to elicit durable broadly neutralizing antibody (bnAb) memory responses in animal models when they are reprogrammed to express these antibodies as functional B cell antigen receptors. This reprogramming requires insertion of antibody cassettes into the native IgH locus for their expression using native cell regulatory elements and heavy chain constant genes. However, concerns over double strand break (DSB)-mediated genome editing dampens the impact of this therapeutic approach. The field of genome editing is instead focusing on developing technologies for precision genome editing, or genome editing without DSBs. Precision editing is even more necessary when evaluating the potential of in vivo B cell editing for IgH reprogramming, where safety is of top priority. In this project, we describe multiple orthogonal genome engineering approaches towards precision gene insertion of bnAbs into the IgH locus, including prime-editing-assisted insertion genome editing (PASSIGE) and CRISPR- free recombineering. We will discuss using a novel method of retron-mediated donor amplification that can enable an all-RNA system for donor-mediated gene insertion. Finally, individualized delivery systems will be evaluated in vitro alongside each editing approach, weighing features including delivery efficacy, safety of both vector and cargo, ease of production, and clinical precedent, with successful systems progressing to in vivo evaluation. Success of this project will enable an off-the-shelf compound for IgH reprogramming with potential as an in vivo administered treatment for HIV infection.

title: A Direct RNA Sequencing Platform to Detect Uridine Modifications in Human Lung Cancer Transcripts
text:
This project will develop a sequencing platform to distinguish dihydrouridine (D) from other uridine modifications
in human RNAs, with a focus on lung adenocarcinoma. By creating accurate maps of these modifications in
patient tumors, the work will reveal how they influence RNA biology in cancer. These mechanistic insights will
provide a foundation for new therapeutic strategies that target RNA modification pathways.

title: Plasmonic and Evanescent scattering microscopy for label-free functional imaging of single molecular and cellular activities
text:
This project aims to develop advanced near-field optical scattering microscopy technologies for label-free,
functional imaging of molecular and cellular activities. These innovations will enable several critical bioanalytical
applications, including: a label-free, single-molecule digital immunoassay for ultrasensitive detection of molecular
biomarkers directly in complex media, including whole blood; a one-step digital binding kinetics assay for
quantitative, label-free analysis of weak or complex molecular interactions; and label-free cell force microscopy
for non-invasive, real-time monitoring of cellular mechanical dynamics. These novel capabilities will significantly
enhance biomedical research, drug discovery, and clinical diagnostics by providing powerful, non-invasive tools
for molecular and cellular analysis.

title: Multimodal Optical Imaging and AI Analytics to Uncover APOE4 Etiology and Therapeutic Targets in Late Onset Alzheimer's Disease
text:
RELEVANCE
Alzheimer's disease poses a growing public health crisis due to its increasing prevalence and lack of effective
treatments. This research seeks to uncover the early vascular mechanisms by which the APOE4 allele
contributes to Alzheimer's disease pathogenesis, focusing on microvascular dysfunctions that precede amyloid
and tau pathologies. By identifying and targeting these early events, the study aims to develop novel
therapeutic strategies that could delay or prevent disease progression, ultimately reducing the burden of
Alzheimer's disease on individuals and society.

title: Causative mechanisms for keloid formation
text:
In the US, keloids most commonly occur in individuals with African ancestry, are less prevalent in other
populations of color and more rare in Whites. Despite the severe physical, psychological and social impact of
keloids and despite the unsatisfactory treatment success, this wound healing disorder has been understudied
and contributes to racial disparity in research and health care. Keloid research is highly relevant to public
health and is recognized as such by the NIH/NIAMS Strategic Plan for fiscal years 2020-2024.

title: Omni Oblique Plane Microscope to spread light-sheet based imaging in biomedical research
text:
We propose a versatile and flexible light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM)
platform, which will be able to perform a wide range of imaging applications, ranging
from single cells to cleared tissues. LSFM are typically highly specialized instruments,
but we hypothesize that versatility is needed to realize the full potential of LSFM in the
life sciences. To study the efficacy of therapies, we will image calcium signaling and
cytoskeletal structure in human derived cardiomyocytes, highlighting the adaptability
and potential of our instrument in biomedical research.

title: Targeting Renalase for early stage T1D treatment
text:
Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is caused by autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing pancreatic beta cells, and
current treatments cannot provide the precise glycemic control of functional beta cells and prevent diabetes
complications. This research focuses on the studying of Renalase (RNLS), a new discovered target gene for
early-stage T1D, aiming to protect beta cells from stress and autoimmune attacks. By developing new drugs
that inhibit RNLS, we hope to prevent beta cell loss and potentially delay or stop T1D progression.

title: Defining the Impact of Tumor Heterogeneity in Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma
text:
Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is a cancer of the bile ducts with a devastating 9% 5-year survival rate
and few therapeutic options. A critical gap in knowledge needed to improve outcomes in iCCA is the impact of
tumor heterogeneity on disease progression, therapeutic failure, and metastatic seeding. This proposal aims to
determine alterations in the genome, transcriptome, and tumor microenvironment that contribute to tumor
heterogeneity, cancer evolution, and adaptation in iCCA with the ultimate goal of accelerating development of
more efficacious treatment strategies.

title: Neurocognitive and Patient-Reported Outcomes after Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Therapy: A Controlled Comparison
text:
Long-term survivorship is now a real possibility for patients with relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma
(LBCL) treated with the chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy. Almost nothing is known about
neurocognitive and patient-reported outcomes in patients undergoing this treatment, however. The current study
will investigate longitudinal changes in these outcomes in the first year after CAR T-cell therapy compared to
individuals without cancer.

title: Repurposing LNP technology to simplify gene editing in nematodes
text:
This project seeks to leverage lipid nanoparticle technology to make mutations in the model organism C. ele-
gans using genome editing. Specifically, we propose to develop a new mutagenesis pipeline—termed LNP-
CRISPR—that enables delivery of genome editing reagents without microinjection. If successful, the approach
will eliminate a major bottleneck to high throughput gene function studies and will enable editing om labs that
lack the expertise or equipment perform traditional microinjection.

title: Role of beta2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in the insula-BNST pathway in ethanol consumption and abstinence-induced negative affect.
text:
Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a severe health crisis that is characterized by detrimental effects to social
relationships and personal wellbeing. The insula-BNST pathway has been implicated in driving AUD-
associated behavior, including abstinence-induced negative affect-like behavior and compulsive ethanol
consumption. Evidence suggests that insular α4β2 nAChRs are a highly sensitive target for chronic ethanol;
thus we propose that these receptors expressed in insula-BNST projecting neurons are implicated in ethanol
consumption and negative affect and are a potential therapeutic target for AUD.

title: Genome editing of fructose metabolism to correct hereditary fructose intolerance in mice.
text:
The goal of this research is to find a cure for hereditary fructose intolerance (HFI), a genetic disease triggered
by fructose that is caused by mutations in the aldob gene with serious health implications such as symptomatic
hypoglycemia, liver and kidney disease. Unfortunately, there is no cure for this potentially fatal disease and
treatment is limited to avoid foods with fructose which is very challenging since fructose -as sugar- is added to
up to 70% of processed foods. Using a mouse ortholog model that mimics the disease in humans, we propose
to study two different approaches to treat this condition, to either conditionally repress the ability of tissues to
process fructose or to use in vivo gene editing to repair missense mutations in the aldob gene of adult mice.

title: Modeling Cell Fate and Perturbation Dynamics with Generative AI using Single-cell and Spatial Omics Data
text:
The spatiotemporal dynamics of cells are shaped by a complex interplay of intrinsic and extrinsic factors, creating
nonlinear gene regulatory systems that traditional models struggle to predict. I hypothesize that conditional
generative AI models integrating molecular, spatial, and temporal data can accurately forecast dynamic cellular
behaviors. This proposal builds a virtual cell foundation model to generate transcriptomic trajectories at both
temporal and spatial scales and predict cell fate decisions, disease progression, and therapeutic responses.
